name: EPACK Durable Ltd
title: EPACK Durable Ltd - 544095 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: EPACK Q4 FY26 revenue fell about 8% YoY to Rs 591 crore and EBITDA margin compressed to 4.37%, with a Rs 32.42 crore PLI reversal weighing on the quarter.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 591 crore, down about 8% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 25.8 crore (down about 64% YoY) and a 4.37% margin versus 11.21%. Net profit was Rs 2.4 lakh after a Rs 32.42 crore reversal of PLI income accrued in the first nine months and Rs 21.78 crore of RIPS 2024 incentive recognised in the quarter. For FY26, revenue was Rs 1,894 crore (down 12.7%), EBITDA Rs 113.9 crore (down 27.7%), margin 6.01%, and net profit Rs 3.3 crore. Management said early FY27 trends look better, with industry growth of about 15% expected in Q1 and a strong order book.

financial_highlights.change: of which Rs 4.96 crore relates to FY26 and Rs 16.82 crore to earlier periods
accrued in the nine months to Dec 31, 2025

segments.name: RAC (room air conditioners)
segments.commentary: Q4 RAC revenue fell about 25% YoY, versus about 33% decline in the first three quarters. FY26 RAC utilisation fell to roughly 20-odd% (about 40% by the management's alternative framing) from 45-50% previously; peak-season utilisation fell to about 75% from about 90%.

segments.name: SDA and LDA (small and large domestic appliances)
segments.commentary: Grew about 53% YoY in the quarter, supported by order inflows across existing and new products; air fryers cited as encouraging.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Grew about 50% YoY in the quarter on localisation requirements and deeper customer integration; heat exchangers, injection-moulded parts, PCBs and copper components flagged as priorities.

segments.name: Hisense JV (EPACK Manufacturing Technologies, Sri City)
segments.commentary: Became operational around March 30, 2026 for Hisense-design AC production; washing machine production expected to start around mid-Q2 FY27 after trials.

segments.name: Epavo JV (motors, Bhiwadi)
segments.commentary: New greenfield facility operational since end-Q3 FY26, mass production from January 2026, roughly 3 million motors per annum installed capacity; the JV's losses roughly doubled in FY26 per an analyst, with about Rs 100 crore invested.

guidance_outlook: Industry growth of about 15% expected in Q1 FY27; management said EPACK should outgrow the industry in FY27 but declined to quantify.
Management reiterated a target of about Rs 5,000 crore revenue in the next two to three years.
Asset turn was about 2.6 in FY26 versus 3.2 in FY25; management targets about 4 in the medium to long term.

Normalised gross margin cited at 13-14% and normalised EBITDA around 7%, with improvement expected as utilisation rises; management said historical EBITDA-level stability was 7.5-8.25% over four years.

FY27 is the final year of PLI incentive; the company is eligible for about Rs 60 crore but will not recognise it until revenue thresholds are confirmed. Management said incentives should be treated as above the core margin.
Remaining capex of Rs 170-200 crore planned over the next 9-12 months against a Rs 470 crore budget (Rs 300 crore already capitalised), mainly Bhiwadi and Sri City.
capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 capex about Rs 79 crore, mainly washing machine capacity and component manufacturing; about Rs 300 crore capitalised in the last four quarters against a Rs 470 crore 18-24 month budget.
Remaining capex of Rs 170-200 crore planned over the next 9-12 months, mainly for Bhiwadi and Sri City capacity and new product categories.

Hisense facility at Sri City started production in the last week of March 2026, with AC production scaling for about two months; front-load washing machines under trial with production expected around mid-Q2 FY27.
Epavo Bhiwadi greenfield motor facility capacity about 3 million motors per annum; mass production from January 2026.
Greenfield facility at Bhiwadi expected to contribute meaningfully over coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Management said the post-stabilisation trend from mid-April is strong, with sell-in picking up and trade inventory normalised; industry growth of about 15% expected in Q1 FY27.
Price increases of 15-20% (model-dependent) were passed on by end-March 2026 across commodity, BEE re-rating and geopolitical triggers, with a further increase in April and May.
Management said the industry channel plus brand inventory as of May opening was about 4-4.5 million units, slightly below expected norms.
Customer additions: 17 new customers in FY26 (5 added in Q4) for a total active base of 72; 5 are large multinational cooling customers and the rest are top-10 small domestic appliance players.
Old BEE-rated inventory is not held by EPACK (last shipments by December 31, 2025); management sees no liability on that front.
Compressor sourcing about 60% domestic and 40% imported; government relaxation allows about 30% imports following a May 8 circular.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the PLI benefit reversed and what were the eligibility conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the criteria were investment in the prior year and 5x incremental revenue growth for applicable components; capex was met but incremental revenue shortfall led to reversal of Rs 32.42 crore, pending auditor review and government clarification. The total FY26 eligibility was about Rs 56.5 crore, with only about Rs 32 crore accrued before Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off net effect on profit (around Rs 11-12 crore per an analyst)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is larger: the Rs 32.42 crore reversal plus Rs 24 crore of unrecognised Q4 PLI, leaving a difference of about Rs 35-36 crore versus the full eligibility, after Rs 21 crore of RIPS was booked.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the sharp rise in inventory and payables days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the working-capital build to summer-season inventory, imported compressors stocked ahead of a BIS expiry in mid-April, and payables rising in step; inventory was about Rs 800-837 crore at end-March and management expects normalisation by quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue double in two to three years and will EPACK outgrow the industry in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the Rs 5,000 crore ambition in two to three years and said EPACK should outgrow the roughly 15% industry growth, but gave no numeric guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken and will margins compress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cumulative price increases of 15-20% were taken by end-March, with a further rise in April and May; some lag is expected in Q1, with a Y-o-Y margin squeeze but some sequential improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RAC utilisation level in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annualised utilisation fell to roughly 20-40% (figures given inconsistently) from 45-50% historically; peak-season utilisation fell to about 75% from about 90%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Hisense JV exposed to China-related policy risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPACK funded the Sri City facility itself under a tech-transfer arrangement, sees no policy impact, and expects Hisense to expand into washing machines and other products in Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the auditor qualification about?
qa_highlights.answer: The qualification relates to a Rs 19.61 crore receivable from customer Gangnam, which is sub judice; management said it believes the amount is recoverable and has filed legal complaints.

risks_watch: Quality of earnings: Q4 net profit of Rs 2.4 lakh was after a Rs 32.42 crore PLI reversal and Rs 21.78 crore RIPS income; the PLI reversal could be reinstated, but management said it will wait at least another quarter for clarity.
Working capital: inventory of about Rs 800-837 crore and trade payable days rising to about 130-140 from about 90-100 need to normalise; watch the next quarter's inventory and payables.
Margin pass-through lag from commodity and forex moves, which management said is unpredictable; Q1 FY27 margins still expected below prior-year levels YoY.
Receivable of Rs 19.61 crore from Gangnam under legal dispute and flagged by auditors as a qualification.
Epavo JV losses reportedly doubled in FY26 with about Rs 100 crore invested and a Rs 23 crore loan; breakeven expected only in FY27-28.
Asset turn fell to about 2.6 from 3.2; debt about Rs 700 crore including a Rs 200 crore term loan.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the near-term recovery and long-term ambition, but notably cautious on incentives (PLI, RIPS) and margin pass-through, with several answers deferred or left unquantified. Management gave no numeric guidance on FY27 revenue or margins and was inconsistent on some utilisation and margin figures.
key_quotes: Excluding this one-time impact, the operational performance during Q4 FY26 provides a more normalized reflection of the underlying business performance during the quarter.
So, we will still want to wait for another quarter or so before we get the confirmed intent from the agencies on this.
And we are seeing a very strong pull in the trade.
Any incentive, both in terms of PL I or TLI, should be above it.
We don't see any impact in terms of any policy change or any so-called the Chinese government stand on any such thing.

growth.why: Management expects industry growth of about 15% in Q1 FY27 and says EPACK should outgrow it, but did not quantify; the Rs 5,000 crore revenue vision in 2-3 years is reiterated, backed by Hisense Sri City AC line, washing machine trials (mid-Q2 FY27), Epavo motors and Rs 170-200 crore remaining capex over 9-12 months, with utilisation at about 20%.
